outcome_detail: Two federal class actions were consolidated on October 30, 2025 (B. (PS) v. Aber, No. 1:25-cv-02763, consolidated into lead case Hiehle v. Aber, No. 1:25-cv-02531, D. Colo., Judge Gordon P. Gallagher). Per the Civil Rights Litigation Clearinghouse (as of February 15, 2026), the consolidated litigation remains active with no settlement, dismissal, or class-certification ruling reported. Plaintiffs seek damages, declaratory and injunctive relief, and systemic changes to how strip-search videos are recorded, stored, and accessed.
criminal_detail: Edward Aber was charged in July 2025 with 117 counts of invasion of privacy for sexual gratification and one count of first-degree official misconduct (all misdemeanors), based on a Colorado Bureau of Investigation probe finding he accessed the jail's Evidence.com system 3,166 times, mostly tied to strip-search videos of female inmates, between February 2019 and January 2024. He turned down a plea deal and pleaded not guilty in March 2026; his trial was continued from early August 2026 to November 2026. He resigned from the sheriff's office in July 2024.
incident_date_approx: February 2019 - January 2024 (alleged repeated viewing of strip-search videos), La Plata County Jail, Durango, Colorado
description: Women formerly held at the La Plata County Jail filed federal class-action litigation in the U.S. District Court for the District of Colorado against former jail commander Edward Aber, Sheriff Sean Smith, Lt. Jacob Harris, Sgt. Micheal Slade, and the La Plata County Board of County Commissioners. A first proposed class action was filed in mid-August 2025 on behalf of three women (Hiehle v. Aber), and a second was filed September 3, 2025 on behalf of 18 women proceeding by initials (B. (PS) v. Aber); the cases were consolidated in October 2025. According to the complaints, Aber used his law-enforcement credentials to access the jail's evidence system at least 3,166 times over roughly five years, repeatedly viewing strip-search videos of approximately 115-117 female inmates from his home, office, and hotel rooms for sexual gratification, storing videos and screenshots on personal devices and deleting them when he learned of the investigation. The suits also allege sexual contact with inmates, closed-door meetings with female inmates in his office, prior sexual-harassment complaints from female jail employees, and that the county and sheriff knew of past accusations against Aber and failed to control access to strip-search footage. Aber faces 117 misdemeanor counts of invasion of privacy for sexual gratification and one count of official misconduct; he pleaded not guilty in March 2026 and awaits a November 2026 trial. The civil litigation is ongoing.
notes: Consolidated mass litigation kept as ONE record per rules: Hiehle v. Aber (No. 1:25-cv-02531, filed August 2025, three plaintiffs) and B. (PS) v. Aber (No. 1:25-cv-02763, filed September 3, 2025, 18 plaintiffs) were consolidated October 30, 2025 under lead case 25-cv-02531. Core allegations are sexual privacy violations (voyeuristic viewing of strip-search videos) rather than physical sexual assault, though the complaints also allege sexual contact with inmates and sexual harassment of employees.
